scenes.visual: Title card: Neurons Compete for Limited Support. Show axons converging on a target with a limited supply of yellow survival factor.

scenes.tts: Developing neurons compete for a limited supply of survival factor from their targets. That is the neurotrophic hypothesis. Neurons are made in excess. The target is the tissue an axon grows to and connects with. It supplies the factor. Neurons that get too little die by apoptosis. Competition lets the target's supply decide how many neurons stay alive.

The target is the tissue an axon grows to and connects with. It supplies the factor. Neurons that get too little die by apoptosis. Competition lets the target's supply decide how many neurons stay alive.

scenes.visual: Open on excess blue neurons sending axons to a grey target. Show a limited supply of yellow factor at the target, uptake by axon endings, and unsupported neurons turning red and fading. Label the central idea: competition for limited target-derived support. Do not show neurons being born in response to factor.

scenes.tts: Remove a target, and more neurons die. Add target, and fewer die. In chick spinal ganglia, many neurons formed and grew fibres before dying cells became conspicuous. The neurons were made, then lost.
scenes.narration: Remove a target, and more neurons die. Add target, and fewer die. In chick spinal ganglia, many neurons formed and grew fibres before dying cells became conspicuous. The neurons were made, then lost.
scenes.caption: Remove a target, and more neurons die. Add target, and fewer die. In chick spinal ganglia, many neurons formed and grew fibres before dying cells became conspicuous. The neurons were made, then lost.
scenes.visual: Compare target removal with target addition: more neurons fade when target is removed, fewer when target is added. Then show the chick spinal ganglion time course: neurons form and extend fibres before later degeneration. Keep these as schematic comparisons without numerical labels.

scenes.tts: Nerve growth factor, or N G F, is the test case. Give young mammals extra N G F, and sympathetic ganglia enlarge. Block it with antiserum in newborn mice, and the ganglia waste away. But antibodies might bind something other than N G F.
scenes.narration: Nerve growth factor, or NGF, is the test case. Give young mammals extra NGF, and sympathetic ganglia enlarge. Block it with antiserum in newborn mice, and the ganglia waste away. But antibodies might bind something other than NGF.
scenes.caption: Nerve growth factor, or NGF, is the test case. Give young mammals extra NGF, and sympathetic ganglia enlarge. Block it with antiserum in newborn mice, and the ganglia waste away. But antibodies might bind something other than NGF.
scenes.visual: Show young-mammal sympathetic ganglia enlarging with extra NGF, then newborn-mouse ganglia depleted with anti-NGF serum. Label addition and blockade. Finish on the antibody specificity question; remove the old question about whether NGF decides the number of neurons made.

scenes.tts: Genetics tests that doubt. Mice lacking N G F or its receptor, T R K A, lose sympathetic neurons and many sensory neurons. Without T R K A, the sympathetic ganglion still forms and axons start growing. Later the neurons die. What failed was survival.
scenes.narration: Genetics tests that doubt. Mice lacking NGF or its receptor, TrkA, lose sympathetic neurons and many sensory neurons. Without TrkA, the sympathetic ganglion still forms and axons start growing. Later the neurons die. What failed was survival.
scenes.caption: Genetics tests that doubt. Mice lacking NGF or its receptor, TrkA, lose sympathetic neurons and many sensory neurons. Without TrkA, the sympathetic ganglion still forms and axons start growing. Later the neurons die. What failed was survival.
scenes.visual: Show independent disruption of NGF and TrkA leading to sympathetic and sensory neuron losses. For the TrkA-null sympathetic ganglion, animate initial formation and axon growth, followed by later neuronal loss. Label survival failure; omit the exact embryonic day.

scenes.tts: Add excess N G F during the death period in chick embryos, and more neurons escape the normal death. Count neurons and dying cells, and mark dividing cells to check. Early N G F can also increase division.
scenes.narration: Add excess NGF during the death period in chick embryos, and more neurons escape the normal death. Count neurons and dying cells, and mark dividing cells to check. Early NGF can also increase division.
scenes.caption: Add excess NGF during the death period in chick embryos, and more neurons escape the normal death. Count neurons and dying cells, and mark dividing cells to check. Early NGF can also increase division.
scenes.visual: Show treated and untreated chick ganglia across the death period. Preserve neurons in the treated condition by preventing their fade, without reviving already dead neurons. Show separate readouts for neuron counts, dying cells and division; flag early exposure as a condition that can increase division.

scenes.tts: How does a target support a distant cell body? The factor acts at the axon ending. A signal returns along the axon to the cell body to support survival.
scenes.narration: How does a target support a distant cell body? The factor acts at the axon ending. A signal returns along the axon to the cell body to support survival.
scenes.caption: How does a target support a distant cell body? The factor acts at the axon ending. A signal returns along the axon to the cell body to support survival.
scenes.visual: Zoom from target contact to an axon ending, then track a signal back along the axon to the distant cell body. Label direction: target to cell body. Avoid adding molecular transport details not described in the lesson.

scenes.tts: Dependence varies with population and age. Antiserum has much less effect in older animals. Limb motor neurons do not depend on N G F. Large sensory neurons that sense muscle stretch depend on a different neurotrophin.
scenes.narration: Dependence varies with population and age. Antiserum has much less effect in older animals. Limb motor neurons do not depend on NGF. Large sensory neurons that sense muscle stretch depend on a different neurotrophin.
scenes.caption: Dependence varies with population and age. Antiserum has much less effect in older animals. Limb motor neurons do not depend on NGF. Large sensory neurons that sense muscle stretch depend on a different neurotrophin.
scenes.visual: Compare newborn and older animals under antiserum, with less effect in older animals. Then distinguish NGF-dependent populations from limb motor neurons and large stretch-sensing sensory neurons; show the latter supplied by a different neurotrophin. Do not suggest all neurons require NGF.

scenes.tts: Survival is only part of the story. N G F also promotes axon growth and branching. When sympathetic neurons make their own N G F, axons still reach their tissues but branch sparsely inside them. Keeping neurons alive does not explain their wiring.
scenes.narration: Survival is only part of the story. NGF also promotes axon growth and branching. When sympathetic neurons make their own NGF, axons still reach their tissues but branch sparsely inside them. Keeping neurons alive does not explain their wiring.
scenes.caption: Survival is only part of the story. NGF also promotes axon growth and branching. When sympathetic neurons make their own NGF, axons still reach their tissues but branch sparsely inside them. Keeping neurons alive does not explain their wiring.
scenes.visual: Compare normal target-supplied NGF with NGF made by sympathetic neurons themselves. In both, axons reach the tissue; in the latter, show sparse branching inside it. Keep survival and the pattern of innervation as distinct readouts.

scenes.tts: A smaller closing point: for a fixed population, survival alone cannot save more neurons than were made. Extra factor can spare neurons that would otherwise die.
scenes.narration: A smaller closing point: for a fixed population, survival alone cannot save more neurons than were made. Extra factor can spare neurons that would otherwise die.
scenes.caption: A smaller closing point: for a fixed population, survival alone cannot save more neurons than were made. Extra factor can spare neurons that would otherwise die.
scenes.visual: Label Smaller point: the survival ceiling. Briefly show the same fixed starting population, with extra factor sparing more of it. Cap survivors at the neurons already made. Avoid the old extended equation and graph sequence.
End card: Neurons compete for limited target-derived support. Return to the target and its supported neurons, without repeating the ceiling as the main takeaway.
